title: Add hierarchical contrast prober and visual explainability CI gate
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: We need a finer-grained, semantically-aware probe that can detect prompt-set sensitivity concentrated in localized semantic clusters and present it to engineers as an explainable visual artifact. This PR introduces a Hierarchical Contrast Prober (HCP) that builds semantic clusters, runs structured perturbation probes within clusters, and emits a per-prompt sensitivity score with a summary heatmap. It also adds a CI gate that aggregates sensitivity signals, applies a severity calibration layer to avoid noisy false positives, and uploads both JSON artifacts and a small PNG heatmap to the CI run artifacts for easier triage.

What this PR does (summary):
- new module eval_harness/probers/hierarchical_contrast_prober.py: builds hierarchical semantic clusters using existing embedding pipelines, runs contrastive perturbations at multiple granularities, and computes per-prompt sensitivity and cluster-level impact metrics.
- new visualizer eval_harness/reports/sensitivity_heatmap.py: lightweight matplotlib based generator that produces a compact PNG heatmap and an accompanying JSON with coordinates and explanations. Heatmap is intentionally minimal to be CI-artifact-friendly (no heavy web deps).
- CI hook integration in .ci/hooks/sensitivity_gate.py: loads the JSON signals, applies a calibrated threshold schedule (soft-fail for low-confidence blips, fail-for-severity for consistent regressions), and emits a structured failure message with links to the artifact.
- wiring: small changes to eval orchestration to export probe outputs to artifacts/heatmaps/<run-id>/ and to include a short narrative summary in the PR check output.
- docs: docs/eval-harness/probers.md updated with usage and upgrade notes, plus a quickstart notebook example in examples/contrast_probe_quickstart.ipynb.

Design notes and trade-offs: HCP intentionally reuses the existing embedding infrastructure to avoid new model dependencies. Clustering is a two-stage process (coarse semantic clustering via approximate kmeans + local agglomerative refinement) to keep runtime bounded for large prompt sets. The CI gate uses a calibration curve derived from historical runs (small lookup table in eval_harness/ci/calibration_v1.json) so teams can opt into stricter failure modes. The visualizer is intentionally non-interactive to minimize CI flakiness and artifact size.

Testing and validation:
- unit tests: tests/probers/test_hierarchical_contrast_prober.py covers clustering correctness, perturbation generation, and scoring invariants.
- integration smoke: examples/contrast_probe_quickstart.ipynb and ci/integration/sensitivity_smoke.yml run a small prompt-set and validate artifacts generation.
- historical backfill: a one-off script scripts/backfill_sensitivity.py was used to run the probe against last 30 nightly runs for validation; results used to tune the threshold calibration.

Migration notes:
- No breaking public API changes. Existing probe runners can call the new prober via a new name 'hierarchical_contrast' in the orchestration config.
- Teams that want visual artifacts must opt-in to artifact collection (default off for self-hosted CI to save storage).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: noisy failures for tiny prompt-sets. Mitigation: gate soft-fail by default, require a minimum prompt-set size (configurable) before hard-fail is allowed.
- Risk: added CI time. Mitigation: probe is CPU-granular and can be run as a post-submit artifact generation step; default CI config runs a lightweight cluster pass only.

Related: builds on ideas from ENG-13782 (contrastive probing) and ENG-18731 (prompt sensitivity dashboards).

review_conversation: Miguel Torres: Nice work, this addresses a long-standing blind spot. A couple asks: can we limit worst-case runtime and add a flag for disabling local agglomerative step? Also please add an integration smoke for GH actions (so artifact upload path is validated).

Aisha Kapoor: Thanks Miguel — added a config flag 'refine_clusters' (default false in CI) and the integration smoke workflow at ci/integration/sensitivity_smoke.yml. Also added a runtime cap and a warning log when exceeded.
Renee Park: Tests look good but I hit a flake in CI where matplotlib backend caused headless failures on ubuntu-latest. Suggest switching to Agg backend explicitly in the visualizer.
Aisha Kapoor: Good catch — switched to 'Agg' and added a headless CI run in smoke. Pushed fix in commit d2e1a44.
Benji Clark: Can we make the severity calibration table pluggable? I'd like tenant-specific overrides.
Aisha Kapoor: Calibration table is now pluggable via eval_harness/ci/calibration_v1.json and can be overridden via CI env var EVAL_CALIBRATION_PATH. Documented in prober usage section.
release_notes: Introduces a hierarchical contrast prober and visual CI gate which surfaces per-prompt sensitivity and emits explainability heatmaps as CI artifacts. Default gate is soft-fail; teams can opt into hard-fail by configuring threshold calibration. See docs/eval-harness/probers.md for usage and migration notes.
notes_for_qa: QA should run the integration smoke workflow with a synthesized prompt-set that has injected high-sensitivity prompts (scripts/backfill_sensitivity.py includes a small generator). Verify artifact PNG and JSON are generated and uploaded to the run artifacts. Verify the gate behavior toggles between soft-fail and hard-fail when calibration is changed.
